title: Memo 1: Theory of Regulation
description_html:
Memo 1. Theory of Regulation (due November 3 by 11:59 PM)

Prompt:

In Lecture 2, we discussed the difficulty of constructing a market for clean air and non-rival goods more generally. This raises the free-rider problem: even if someone values clean air, they may refuse to pay for it because they will receive the benefits anyway. 

Can you think of examples from your time at SOM or your work or educational background in which you’ve experienced the free-rider problem? Can you think of examples when you’ve been a free-rider yourself? If you haven’t experienced this personally, can you think of a free-rider problem you’ve heard about within the SOM community? 

Propose an institutional design or regulation to address one of the problems you identified, grounded in the literature on regulation we discussed in class. Consider the challenges Mushfiq encountered in encouraging compliance with the September ban on Chilean hake fishing. How would your proposed regulation be enforced? 

Please submit here if you attended the 10:05 AM (Silver cohort) section.
Do not submit under multiple sections.

title: Homework 4: Double marginalization and vertical contracts
group_note: Small learning team (Silver 1B). One member uploads with all names, cohort and section.
description_html: Group-of-4 written assignment from the Nov 16 lecture. Demand is q = 250 − 50p and manufacturer MC is 0.2. Part 1, vertical integration: quantity, price, profit, consumer surplus and markup. Part 2, double marginalization: the retailer's q*(w), the manufacturer's optimal w, the resulting price, both profits, channel profit, consumer surplus and three markups, and who is worse off. Part 3, contracts: two-part tariff; a retailer outside option of 40 (who bears demand risk?); maximum resale price of 2.6 (show channel profit = 288 for any w in [0.2, 2.6]); quantity forcing at 120 units; then compare the contracts on information and uncertainty. Readings: Pindyck & Rubinfeld, appendix to ch. 11, and CBS '60 Minutes' 'Sticker Shock'.

Please submit your case write-up for Aqualisa Quartz. Please refer to the syllabus for instructions, as well as to the detailed class outline section for discussion questions. Case link is posted under Files.

Individual write-up on 'Aqualisa Quartz: Simply a Better Shower' (HBS 9-502-030, with a supplemental spreadsheet and the Managing Director's Note). Maximum 4 pages, with a heading for each question. Upload it before class. Questions: (1) Is Aqualisa Quartz a good product? Who benefits from the Quartz shower, and how?

(2) Why has the Quartz shower not been selling? Analyze Aqualisa's go-to-market strategy and its challenges.

(3) What should Rawlingson do to generate sales momentum for Quartz? Develop alternative strategies to improve market share.

title: Homework 5: Industry analysis of commercial aircraft (memo and 3 slides)
group_note: Small learning team (Silver 1B). Group number 1 means commercial aircraft manufacturing. No AI on this one. A subset of groups presents in class (10 to 12 minutes).
description_html:
No AI allowed. In your group of 4, prepare an industry analysis of Commercial Aircraft Manufacturing following the template in the readings, and state and justify your geographic scope. Answer: (1) are there distinct segments, and does the analysis differ by segment?

(2) which factor most impedes profitability, and why?

(3) the impact of COVID-19, OR of higher global tariffs. Upload a 2–3 page memo and a 3-slide presentation to Canvas. In class (4:10 PM), some groups will be called on to present for at most 10–12 minutes, and other groups will ask questions. Decide who speaks, and have a no-login share link ready (e.g., a tinyurl).

title: Prep: antitrust questions (FTC v. Amazon)
description_html:
Read the FTC Guide to Antitrust Laws excerpts (assembled by AIAG, posted on Canvas) and skim the 2023 FTC v. Amazon complaint. Prepare answers to: (1) What is antitrust law for? Is substantial market power, or even monopoly, illegal? What separates aggressive competition from unlawful anticompetitive conduct?

(2) Why do horizontal and vertical mergers raise different concerns, and what benefits could justify them?

(3) What are the FTC's main allegations, and how do Amazon's alleged practices relate to the competitive strategies discussed in class?

(4) Is the FTC's case persuasive? What separates Amazon's conduct from legitimate efforts to build and sustain competitive advantage? Not turned in.

title: Homework 6: Airline strategies from accounting data (Allegiant vs. Frontier)
group_note: Small learning team (Silver 1B); group 1 gets Allegiant and Frontier. Two people per airline collect data individually, then the group writes a memo (3 pages plus exhibits). No AI, no analyst reports.
description_html: A substantial assignment: start early. AI is not allowed, and neither are analyst reports. In the group, two people take Allegiant and two take Frontier. Each person collects operating and financial data individually, from EDGAR, the 10-K, FAA data and similar sources, and does not collect it together with anyone. Then check and reconcile the numbers with your airline partner. As a group, pick a few cost, operational or quality metrics. Build graphs and tables that contrast the two airlines; Tufte is optional reading for presentation. Write a memo of at most 3 pages of text, plus exhibits, on how the airlines differ and how those differences connect to each firm's overall strategy. Prepare a 10-minute presentation of your findings in case your group is chosen to present in class.

sources.quote: Groups 1 & 2:           Allegiant & Frontier
This is a substantial assignment. We recommend that you start early.
For the airline project, collect data individually before working together.
